newsitem.title: USA: NHL ICE HOCKEY - DEVILS BEAT LIGHTNING FOR FIRST ROAD WIN OF SEASON.
newsitem.headline: NHL ICE HOCKEY - DEVILS BEAT LIGHTNING FOR FIRST ROAD WIN OF SEASON.

text.p: Martin Brodeur stopped 30 shots and his teammates gave him a season-high four goals to work with as the New Jersey Devils picked up their first road win of the season on Saturday.
Dave Andreychuk had a goal and an assist to lead the Devils to a 4-1 victory over the Tampa Bay Lightning.
Bob Carpenter, Randy McKay and Bill Guerin scored the other goals for the Devils, who had combined for only three goals in their first two road games.
"I was very happy with what I saw tonight," said New Jersey coach Jacques Lemaire. "We were very intense."

Brodeur had his shutout bid broken up by Shawn Burr 73 seconds into the third period. Brodeur shut the Lightning down the rest of the way. "This was a big win for us," he said. "It was a confidence-builder."
In Montreal, Saku Koivu and Stephane Richer each scored twice and Martin Rucinsky added a goal and two assists as the Canadiens held on for a 6-5 win over the Philadelphia Flyers.

Richer's goal with 6:22 left in the second snapped a 3-3 tie and Montreal extended its lead to 5-3 at 4:15 of the third on Koivu's second goal of the game. After Philadelphia cut the deficit to one, Richer again beat Ron Hextall to restore the two-goal lead.
Pat Jablonski made 37 saves for the Habs, who were outshot 42-23.
In Edmonton, Rene Corbet's goal with 6:51 remaining snapped a tie and Patrick Roy made 25 saves in his 600th career game as the Colorado Avalanche beat the Oilers 4-2.

Edmonton had rallied from a 2-0 deficit with a pair of second-period goals. But in the third, defenceman Adam Foote sent a centering pass in front to Corbet, who batted the puck out of the air past goaltender Curtis Joseph.
Roy made 28 saves and Valeri Kamensky scored on a penalty shot for the Avalanche.

In Buffalo, Robert Smehlik had two goals and an assist and Pat LaFontaine added a goal and two assists as the Sabres skated to a 6-3 win over the Hartford Whalers to run their winning streak to four games.
Dominik Hasek made 26 saves to earn his 100th NHL win and Alexei Zhitnik set up three goals for Buffalo.

In Boston, Chris Osgood made 23 saves and red-hot Brendan Shanahan scored the winning goal early in the third period as the Detroit Red Wings edged the Bruins 2-1 to run their unbeaten streak to five games.
Shanahan picked up his sixth goal in four games when he scored off a goalmouth scramble 28 seconds into the third for a 2-0 lead.
Osgood lost his shutout bid with 15:02 left when Don Sweeney's slap shot eluded him through traffic.
In Toronto, Mats Sundin scored twice and Felix Potvin made 31 saves as the Maple Leafs beat the Phoenix Coyotes 5-2.

Sundin broke a 2-2 deadlock in the third period with his second goal of the game when he took a pass from Doug Gilmour and beat Nikolai Khabibulin at the 11:20 mark. It was the first powerplay goal allowed by the Coyotes in 32 chances.
Wendel Clark added an insurance tally 2:26 later.
In Dallas, Mike Modano scored twice and Andy Moog made 21 saves as the Stars rolled past the Ottawa Senators 5-1 for their eighth win in 10 games.

Modano scored a short-handed goal in the second period, stealing an errant clearing pass from Ottawa goaltender Damian Rhodes and blasting the puck past him for a 2-0 lead. He made it 4-0 at 10:46 of the third.
Moog lost his shutout bid 94 seconds later when Dave Hannan snapped a shot just under the Dallas crossbar.
On Long Island, Michal Sykora and Owen Nolan scored third period goals to lift the San Jose Sharks into a 2-2 tie with the New York Islanders.
The Sharks were frustrated by Islander goaltender Tommy Salo for more than 49 minutes before breaking through. Nolan's powerplay goal with 5:35 left tied the game.
Sala made 39 saves as San Jose outshot the Isles 41-27.
In St Louis, Jason Allison scored twice as the Washington Capitals scored five unanswered goal to stun the Blues 6-4.

Brett Hull had a goal and three assists as the Blues raced to a 4-1 lead just over 12 minutes into the game. But Andrew Brunette scored a powerplay goal on a deflection with five minutes to go in the first to spark the Caps' comeback.
Allison tied it 4-4 at 2:26 of the second with his second of the game and Dale Hunter put a shot through Grant Fuhr's pads for the game winner.
In Los Angeles, the Kings and Calgary Flames skated to the NHL's first scoreless tie in two seasons.
The Kings' Stephane Fiset made 35 saves and Calgary's Trevor Kidd turned back 26 shots as each picked up his second shutout of the season and eighth career shutout.
An apparent goal by Calgary rookie Jonas Hoglund with 4:12 left in the first period was nullified when referee Dan Marouelli called Flames centre Dave Gagner for goaltender interference.
In Vancouver, Mike Ridley had a goal and an assist and Corey Hirsch made 26 saves as the Canucks edged the Pittsburgh Penguins 2-1, handing them their seventh straight road loss.
Martin Gelinas and Ridley beat Ken Wregget in the first period to stake Vancouver to a 2-0 lead.
Jaromir Jagr scored Pittsburgh's lone goal at 4:11 of the second period. Hirsch stopped 10 Penguins shots in the final period.
